confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear, premeditated pattern of an insider threat. The user (user_03) transitioned from normal departmental file reading to systematic cross-departmental access and eventually to bulk data downloading across multiple departments (Legal, Marketing, Finance, Sales, DevOps, and Logs) over several days.

attack_chain.description: User_03 logs in from their normal IP during normal hours.
User_03 begins exploring unauthorized directories, accessing Legal department files.
User_03 expands scope to Marketing department files.
User_03 accesses Finance department files outside of normal working hours.
User_03 transitions from reading to active downloading of files across Sales and Marketing departments, often during off-hours.
User_03 performs bulk downloads of sensitive files from DevOps, Logs, and Marketing departments.

gaps: Lack of information regarding whether user_03 had any legitimate reason or temporary permission to access these directories.
No information on the destination of the downloaded files (e.g., external IP or USB).
narrative: User_03, an HR specialist, exhibited a classic insider threat pattern by gradually expanding their access scope from HR files to Legal, Marketing, Finance, Sales, and DevOps directories. The activity escalated from simple file reads to a high volume of file downloads across multiple departments, frequently occurring during off-hours, indicating premeditated data exfiltration.
